_comment: Servana RUNTIME screen register (Plan §27.3): what is BUILT. Single source of truth; inventory.yaml is generated from this and specs are generated by scripts/generate-screen-specs.mjs. Enforced by screenInventory.spec.ts. The REQUIRED authenticated page contract is a separate register — docs/frontend/navigation/servana-user-account-navigation-map.yaml (160 pages). UI-01 established that the two registers are reconciled, never summed. Status vocabulary follows UI/UX plan §7.2: implemented | planned | disabled_by_gate | removed_by_authority.

screens.title: Public account landing page
screens.summary: The resolved account host's own public landing page: sixteen semantic regions built from that account's compiled content, curated imagery, approved factual trust evidence, role-appropriate plan access and registry-derived calls to action.

screens.title: Not found
screens.summary: Catch-all route stating plainly that the address does not exist on this account host, with links to that host's home page and FAQ. It previously rendered the entry card, which made every wrong path look like a working page.

screens.title: Design system demo
screens.summary: Internal design-system gallery used for visual and a11y verification.

screens.title: Legal document
screens.summary: Compatibility route for the pre-UI-06 /legal/:role/:doc shape. A role equal to the resolved host account redirects to the canonical role-free path; any other role fails closed and renders nothing.

screens.title: Access denied
screens.summary: Role-safe denial state reached by the account-entry guard. Names no account or resource, never redirects to another account, and offers only sign-out plus the contexts the server says the user may enter.

screens.title: Magic Link request
screens.summary: Request a Magic Link by email; uniform 202 response.

screens.title: Merchant self-registration
screens.summary: The only merchant-creation path: a Merchant Administrator self-registers the business account.

screens.title: Check your email
screens.summary: Confirmation that a Magic Link was sent.

screens.title: Magic Link verify
screens.summary: Consumes a Magic Link token and routes to setup or the role landing.

screens.title: MFA enrollment
screens.summary: Mandatory-MFA TOTP enrollment with one-time recovery codes.

screens.title: MFA / step-up challenge
screens.summary: Per-session MFA / step-up challenge via TOTP or recovery code.

screens.title: Staff invitation acceptance
screens.summary: Invited staff accept their invitation via an emailed token.

screens.title: First-time setup
screens.summary: Owner first-time setup wizard gating dashboard access.

screens.title: Super Administrator landing
screens.summary: Live Super Administrator role home with header navigation, actions, FAQ, and legal footer.

screens.title: Super Administrator get started
screens.summary: Contract page §5.4.2. Seven configuration steps in dependency order, evidenced by SIX shipped reads (billing settings, plans with nested prices and entitlements, preferred-personnel fee rules, SMS billing settings, registration monitor, MFA status) composed with Promise.allSettled so one unreadable endpoint degrades only its own step. The Wallet and Refer & Earn step is blocked by External Gate W, is never manually completable, and is excluded from the completion denominator.

screens.summary: Live Merchant Administrator role home with sidebar navigation, actions, FAQ, and legal footer.

screens.title: Branch detail
screens.summary: Retired in favor of merchant.branch-detail for owner oversight and branch.branch-profile for the assigned Branch Manager context.

screens.summary: Guided get-started checklist for Audit.

screens.title: Branch audit log
screens.summary: Read-only, branch-scoped, field-masked audit event list with allowlisted severity/action/date filters, sort, and pagination; merchant-level (branch_id null) rows are never shown; no raw before/after/context.

screens.title: Audit event detail
screens.summary: Immutable, read-only audit record with safe actor/subject summaries and masked context; no source-mutation controls, no ids/hashes/paths/signed URLs/tokens/unmasked PII.

screens.title: Flagged events
screens.summary: Branch-scoped flagged-event queue across open/under_review/resolved/dismissed/reopened with status filter, assignee and review-status summaries, and timestamps.

screens.title: Flagged event review
screens.summary: Flagged-event review: start-review/resolve/dismiss/reopen gated by the server capability map and current state, with required review notes, terminal-transition confirmation, and invalid-transition errors; the source event stays read-only.

screens.title: Finance audit
screens.summary: Read-only, branch-scoped, masked finance-domain audit view (Audit via audit.finance.view; Finance via finance.audit.view with server MFA); not a Finance operational screen.

screens.title: Compensation audit
screens.summary: Read-only, branch-scoped, masked compensation-domain audit view; honest empty state until the owning phases (20F-20H) emit events; no compensation events/routes/data fabricated.

screens.title: Audit exports
screens.summary: Audit export list + branch-scoped reason-gated request form (fresh step-up server-enforced; no unassigned/merchant-level export); never exposes file_id/paths/signatures/internal ids/raw failure messages.

screens.title: Audit export detail
screens.summary: Export detail with queued/processing/ready/failed/expired/revoked polling, private on-demand signed download (never stored; accounting changes after stream), and authorized revoke with confirmation.

screens.title: Unsupported role state
screens.summary: Fail-safe boundary when an active role identity cannot be resolved.

screens.title: No branch assignment state
screens.summary: Branch-scoped role landing state when no branch is assigned yet.

screens.title: Business profile
screens.summary: Merchant Administrator views and edits the merchant business profile, uploads or replaces its private scanned logo, previews invoice/receipt branding, and sees safe replacement metadata. Business name, slug, country, service-fee tier and every billing/lifecycle column remain read-only context.

screens.title: Merchant branches
screens.summary: Tenant-wide branch directory with entitlement-aware creation and canonical owner detail links.

screens.title: Merchant branch detail
screens.summary: Scoped owner oversight for one branch with explicit Branch Manager, HR, Front Office and Finance responsibility boundaries and no operational override.

screens.title: Staff overview and lifecycle
screens.summary: Paginated tenant-wide safe membership projection with Branch Manager/HR invitation, lifecycle impact confirmation, session counts and branch/status history; phone and client data are absent.

screens.title: Subscription dashboard
screens.summary: Subscription lifecycle status + independent merchant billing status, current plan/price, billing interval, trial + current-period dates, pending scheduled change, latest invoice summary, and a billing read-only explanation. Read-only; backend authoritative.

screens.title: Plan management
screens.summary: Available plans + effective prices, current plan, schedule/cancel a NO-PRORATION next-cycle change with a server-computed effective date (no client-supplied/immediate change). Mutation controls removed in billing read-only; EnsureBillingMutable is authoritative. Structured 409/422 surfaced.

screens.title: Subscription invoices
screens.summary: Invoice list/detail (number, period, plan/price snapshot, amounts/currency/balance, status, issued/due dates, payment-reference-pending). Generate PDF is a mutation blocked in billing read-only; download of an existing PDF is a read allowed in read-only. NO Wallet/STK/PayBill-Till/provider/payment UI.

screens.title: Subscription invoice detail
screens.summary: Immutable merchant-to-Servana invoice snapshot with private PDF generation/download and an exact External Gate W treatment in place of payment initiation or success.

screens.title: Merchant reports
screens.summary: All-branch reports.

screens.title: Compensation summary
screens.summary: Masked merchant-wide, currency-grouped compensation liabilities and payout-run status. The Merchant Administrator never configures compensation, creates or verifies a payout run, or marks one paid.

screens.title: High-value payout approvals
screens.summary: Dedicated high-value approval queue using the existing fresh-step-up, idempotency, maker/checker and audit authority. No payout preparation, verification or mark-paid controls.

screens.title: Exceptional period-reopen approvals
screens.summary: Merchant Administrator exceptional period-reopen approvals: lists exception-required period locks with a pending Finance reopen request and an 'Approve reopen' action. The approver must differ from the Finance requester (backend-enforced). The Merchant Administrator holds ONLY exceptional-reopen approval — NO routine locking or reopen execution controls appear here (those are Finance).

screens.title: Merchant account and security
screens.summary: Own-scope identity, verified email, mandatory MFA, Magic Link sessions, theme preference and account-context switching with Merchant-specific wording and no password controls.

screens.title: Branch dashboard
screens.summary: Live assigned-branch operating home with server-derived readiness, day state, workload, cash-up, catalogue, and performance facts.

screens.title: Branch profile
screens.summary: Assigned-branch identity, contact, address, category and status context with branch-scoped profile management authority.

screens.title: Operating calendar
screens.summary: Canonical Branch account route for weekly operating hours, split sessions and date-specific branch calendar exceptions.

screens.title: Branch day operations
screens.summary: Server-authoritative branch business-day state machine with explicit opening, closing and unresolved close-blocker treatment.

screens.title: Staff and availability overview
screens.summary: Read-only assigned-branch personnel readiness, availability and scheduling context without taking over HR assignment authority.

screens.title: Queue read view
screens.summary: Read-only branch queue monitoring that preserves Front Office ownership of assignment and transfer actions.

screens.title: Appointments read view
screens.summary: Read-only visibility of current and future assigned-branch appointments without Front Office scheduling controls.

screens.title: Invoices read view
screens.summary: Paginated branch-scoped invoice status and revenue visibility with every invoice mutation capability explicitly absent.

screens.title: Payment records read view
screens.summary: Paginated branch-scoped payment-record status visibility without recording, validation, rejection or reference-correction authority.

screens.title: Receipts read view
screens.summary: Assigned-branch receipt visibility after Finance validation with no issue, reissue or validation controls.

screens.title: Branch audit log
screens.summary: Paginated read-only branch audit-event projection that complements, but does not replace, the dedicated Audit account.

screens.title: Branch account and preferences
screens.summary: Own-scope identity, verified email, MFA, Magic Link sessions, theme preference and account-context switching with Branch wording and no passwords.

screens.title: Service catalogue
screens.summary: Branch Manager service catalogue: list/filter, create/edit (price in minor units, duration, category), archive with confirmation, and a read-only eligibility view. Contact-free; the legacy preferred-personnel fee is never shown or editable.

screens.title: Service eligibility
screens.summary: HR manages which personnel are eligible for each service within HR's assigned branch: select a service, assign/revoke eligible personnel (same-branch only).

screens.title: Availability
screens.summary: HR manages personnel availability within its branch: weekly working days, split shifts, recurring breaks, date-specific exceptions, days off, and emergency unavailability, with a required change reason. Atomic replacement; derived current state and eligible-services summary shown; times in Africa/Nairobi. No-permission and no-branch boundaries.

screens.title: Personnel schedule
screens.summary: Retired in favor of the canonical UI-10 branch.staff route, which preserves this read-only schedule and availability behavior.

screens.title: Appointments (read-only)
screens.summary: Retired in favor of the canonical UI-10 branch.operations-appointments route, which preserves the same read-only authority boundary.

screens.title: Queue (read-only)
screens.summary: Retired in favor of the canonical UI-10 branch.operations-queue route, which preserves the same read-only authority boundary.

screens.title: Queue settings
screens.summary: Branch Manager queue configuration on today's Branch Day: open/close the queue, set capacity (cannot be below the current active count), and set the default assignment mode (next available or manual). Not an operational entry mutation; the backend enforces branch.profile.manage + day.open_close.

screens.title: Branch calendar
screens.summary: Retired in favor of the canonical UI-10 branch.branch-calendar route, which preserves the completed date-exception behavior.

screens.title: Cash-up and reconciliation
screens.summary: Branch Manager cash-up (maker): a business-date branch-day cash-up with one line per concrete payment method. Expected amounts are SERVER-derived and never editable; the Branch Manager enters counted amounts, sees per-method + total variance, saves a draft, and submits for Finance review (or resubmits after a correction request). Submitted / approved / locked cash-ups are read-only. The Branch Manager can NEVER approve — approval is Finance, backend-enforced. No-branch boundary shown when unassigned.

screens.title: Branch reports
screens.summary: Branch reports.

screens.title: Compensation
screens.summary: Branch-scoped, HR-only compensation-plan and commission-rule configuration: plan list with status/backdated/pending-approval indicators, plan detail with append-only history, commission-rule and plan draft forms (F1 model shape, F4 value shape, preferred-personnel-fee basis inclusion), and the named submit/approve/reject/cancel transitions (approval requires a fresh step-up and a different approver). Phase 20G §9.1: a selected_services commission-rule draft shows a branch-scoped service multi-select whose options load from the narrow compensation-scoped GET /commission-rule-service-options endpoint (authorized by compensation.plan.view, never service.view which HR cannot hold; returns {ulid,name} for the acting branch's active services only) — at least one service required, add/remove only while draft, server-returned selections hydrate, stale selection cleared when applies_to changes, non-draft memberships read-only; selected_service_ulids are submitted and the server persists immutable draft memberships. Configuration only — no earned commission, salary ledger, commission ledger, payout, earnings statement, liability or Wallet/provider surface exists here.

screens.title: Payout runs
screens.summary: Branch-scoped HR payout DRAFT workflow: list/filter payout runs, create a run for a branch + pay period + currency (Servana snapshots the eligible earned salary/commission/adjustments server-side — the browser never enters amounts or items), edit a draft (re-snapshot), submit (freeze + claim ledgers), and cancel a draft. HR never verifies, approves, or marks paid (Plan §10.2). Invalid transitions surface a safe state; the browser computes no authoritative total. Servana moves no money; no Wallet/provider UI.

screens.title: Finance task inbox
screens.summary: Capability-gated Finance home surfacing everything awaiting action: payment groups pending validation or requiring correction, refunds awaiting approval / finalization, disputes open or under review, cash-ups awaiting review, period reopen requests, and exports queued/processing/failed. Each tile is shown only when the role holds the relevant capability and links to its full surface. Counts are UX only; the backend is the authoritative boundary.

screens.title: Pending validations
screens.summary: Finance list of payment recording groups awaiting a whole-group decision (branch-scoped, masked). Opens the payment-recording detail where Finance validates the whole group (one original receipt), rejects or requests correction (mandatory reason, no receipt), corrects a component reference, and resubmits. No partial-component validation; the recording maker can never validate their own group (backend-enforced).

screens.title: Receipts
screens.summary: Finance receipt list (branch-scoped): receipt number, invoice, server-formatted KES amount, reissue badge, and readiness. Receipts are issued AUTOMATICALLY on validation; there is no manual issue action.

screens.title: Receipt detail
screens.summary: Immutable receipt + snapshot components. Finance may REISSUE (a new gap-free number referencing the original; mandatory reason) and DOWNLOAD via a short-lived authorized signed link (used immediately, never stored). No manual issue action.

screens.title: External refunds
screens.summary: Finance external-refund list with a status filter and a capability-gated 'Request refund' form (against a validated component; amount capped server-side at the remaining refundable; masked external reference). Servana never moves funds — a refund records the intent.

screens.title: Refund detail
screens.summary: Refund detail showing the refunded component, masked external reference, maker/checker state, and status. A DISTINCT Finance membership approves + finalizes (both require a fresh step-up, server-enforced); finalization is IRREVERSIBLE and reduces the recognised invoice balance, with an explicit warning. Period-lock (423) errors are surfaced verbatim.

screens.title: Disputes
screens.summary: Finance dispute list with a status filter and a capability-gated 'Open dispute' form linked to an invoice and/or a payment record. The disputed source record is never mutated by the investigation.

screens.title: Dispute detail
screens.summary: Move a dispute open → under_review → resolved/rejected (resolution/rejection need a mandatory note). The linked invoice/payment is READ-ONLY here; private evidence downloads via an authorized signed link.

screens.title: Cash-up review
screens.summary: Finance cash-up review inbox (branch-scoped): business date, server-derived expected + counted totals, and variance per submitted cash-up. Opens the review detail.

screens.title: Cash-up review detail
screens.summary: Cash-up detail with per-method expected/counted/variance lines. Finance (checker) approves, rejects, or requests correction of a submitted cash-up, and locks an approved one. The branch manager who submitted can never approve (backend actor guard). Expected totals are server-derived; the submitted snapshot is not overwritten.

screens.title: Financial periods
screens.summary: Finance financial-period locks: create a merchant-wide or branch lock (optionally exception-required), and run a controlled reopen (request reason → execute with a fresh step-up). An exceptional reopen waits for a distinct Merchant Administrator approval before Finance may execute. A locked period blocks applicable mutations with 423; reads/receipts/disputes/exports are never locked.

screens.title: Exports
screens.summary: Finance exports: request a scoped, masked export (a fresh step-up is server-enforced; only invoices/payments/receipts/cash_up/refunds/disputes are offered — compensation/payouts/billing are not), track status, download a ready export via a short-lived authorized signed link (never stored), and revoke. Download accounting is server-side.

screens.title: Payout runs
screens.summary: Merchant-scoped Finance payout worklist: list/filter runs, verify a submitted run (Servana routes high-value runs to the Merchant Administrator), approve an ordinary run, reject (releasing the claimed liabilities via a reason), and mark an approved run PAID after an EXTERNAL settlement (external payment reference + a not-in-the-future paid date). Verify/approve/mark-paid are financial mutations — fresh step-up + Idempotency-Key are server-enforced; the mark-paid dialog states plainly that Servana records an external payment and moves no money. The raw external reference is never displayed after saving; the browser computes no authoritative total. No provider/Wallet/settlement UI.

screens.title: Earnings queries
screens.summary: Finance earnings-query responder worklist: list/filter the merchant-scoped query queue and resolve or reject a query staff raised about their own earnings. An optional monetary correction on a resolve is recorded as a SEPARATE additive compensation adjustment (a direction-selector -> signed amount_minor float-free parser; a preview stating it does not edit the original earnings) — the original ledger fact is never rewritten and there is no direct ledger edit. Respond is a financial mutation (Idempotency-Key server-enforced; a replay never duplicates the correction); a terminal query shows a read-only resolved/rejected state. No Wallet/provider UI.

screens.title: Invoices
screens.summary: Finance invoice list (branch-scoped, masked client): invoice number/'Draft', total, and status badge. Finance holds invoice.view but NOT invoice.create — no 'New invoice' button is shown.

screens.title: Invoice detail
screens.summary: Finance invoice detail with the additive void/adjust workflow: capability-gated Void (request → confirm execute / reject) and Adjust controls, each requiring a mandatory reason and showing an irreversible-action warning. Finance MFA + fresh step-up on void are enforced by the API; original snapshots and the number are never rewritten.

screens.title: Clients
screens.summary: Front Office client directory + search by name or phone (branch/tenant-scoped). Contact is ALWAYS masked (phone last-four, masked email); the blind index is never shown.

screens.title: Add client
screens.summary: Create a client (name, phone, optional email/notes). A same-branch duplicate phone returns a deterministic conflict linking to the existing record.

screens.title: Client detail
screens.summary: Masked client detail with edit (name/phone/email/notes) and SMS-consent opt-in/out capture (no SMS sent in this phase).

screens.title: Appointments
screens.summary: Front Office appointment list for a chosen business date (branch-scoped): client, service, assigned personnel, status badge, start/end time, with date navigation and status filtering. Create button gated by appointment.create. Walk-ins/queue/sessions are later phases and are not shown here.

screens.title: Book appointment
screens.summary: Book an appointment: pick a branch-scoped client and active service, choose a start time (server-calculated duration/end-time preview), optionally pick a preferred and/or assigned eligible personnel member with availability/conflict feedback. The backend derives merchant/branch/end-time/status; no fee is calculated.

screens.title: Appointment detail
screens.summary: Appointment detail with capability-gated actions as confirmation dialogs: assign/transfer eligible personnel, reschedule, check in the client, cancel (reason required after check-in), and mark no-show. Status badge + transition controls driven by the API capability map; client contact is masked.

screens.title: Queue board
screens.summary: Front Office queue board (branch-scoped): position, masked client, service, assignment mode, assigned/preferred personnel, status badge, and labelled wait estimate. Capability-map-gated controls — assign next available, call, start, complete, mark no-show, and keyboard-accessible move-up/move-down reorder of waiting entries. Start-a-walk-in button gated by queue.create.

screens.title: Start a walk-in
screens.summary: Accessible walk-in wizard: find an existing branch client or create one through the existing client workflow, select an active service, choose the assignment mode, select personnel where required, and confirm. Creates the walk-in and queue entry atomically; the wait estimate is server-calculated and labelled. No preferred-personnel fee is shown or charged.

screens.title: Queue entry detail
screens.summary: Queue-entry detail with capability-gated actions as dialogs: assign/transfer eligible personnel (reason required for transfer), call, start, complete, mark no-show, and cancel (reason required). Status badge + controls driven by the API capability map; client contact is masked.

screens.title: Service sessions
screens.summary: Front Office service-session list (branch-scoped): status, masked client, service, assigned personnel, and a preferred-personnel-override indicator. Start/complete are driven by the queue board; this view owns service-notes editing and cancellation of a pending session (reason required). Completed sessions show the typed NON-PAYABLE commission preview labelled 'Preview — not earned or payable' (never a zero amount when not configured). No invoice, payment, receipt, fee-rule, earned/payable commission, or payout control appears here.

screens.title: Invoices
screens.summary: Front Office invoice list (branch-scoped): invoice number or 'Draft', masked client, server-formatted KES total, and status badge. A capability-gated 'New invoice' button (invoice.create) opens the draft builder. No payment or receipt control appears here (Phase 18).

screens.title: New invoice
screens.summary: Front Office draft builder: select one or more COMPLETED service sessions that share a client (cross-client sources are disabled), then create a draft. The backend derives every price, preferred-personnel fee, currency, and total under lock — the browser never supplies authoritative money. No invoice number is allocated until finalization.

screens.title: Invoice detail
screens.summary: Invoice detail with masked client, itemized services, a separately-shown preferred-personnel fee, subtotal/discount/tax/total, validated-paid and balance. A draft shows a capability-gated Finalize action (confirmation: allocates the number and locks amounts); finalized invoices show a read-only snapshot note. No payment or receipt control appears here.

screens.title: Payments
screens.summary: Front Office payments entry: lists issued/partially-paid invoices (invoice.view) with a 'Record a payment' action each. Recording is not validation and issues no receipt.

screens.title: Record a payment
screens.summary: Front Office recording form (maker): shows the invoice total, masked client, and amount available to record; builds one or more concrete-method components (cash/mpesa_offline/bank_transfer/card_terminal/voucher/other) with method-aware evidence fields and a running total; a single-currency, positive-amount, no-overpayment guard; an explicit confirmation; an idempotency key; a pending-validation success state; and a duplicate-suspected warning. No validation, receipt, or paid-status control. The server derives all authoritative money/status.

screens.title: Receipts
screens.summary: Front Office receipt list (branch-scoped, view only): receipt number, invoice, server-formatted KES amount, readiness. Front Office may VIEW and DOWNLOAD receipts but NEVER reissue, validate, refund, approve, or issue — those controls are absent for this role (backend-enforced).

screens.title: Receipt detail
screens.summary: Front Office receipt detail: immutable receipt + snapshot components with a DOWNLOAD action (short-lived authorized signed link, never stored). No reissue control appears for Front Office (it requires receipt.reissue, which Front Office does not hold).

screens.title: Payment records
screens.summary: Finance read-only list of payment recording groups awaiting action (branch-scoped, masked): invoice number, maker, total, and status (pending validation / held for duplicate review). No validation, rejection, receipt, or refund control (Phase 18B).

screens.title: Payment record detail
screens.summary: Finance payment-recording detail with masked components and, when the group is held for a duplicate reference, a capability-gated override (customer_payment.duplicate_override) with a mandatory reason. The API also enforces MFA + a fresh step-up and never edits the original reference. No validation, rejection, or receipt control (Phase 18B).

screens.title: Finance audit
screens.summary: The Finance role's own MFA-gated, branch-scoped, masked read of the finance-domain audit trail (finance.audit.view; distinct from the Audit role's audit.finance.view). Read-only: no operational mutation and no flagged-review controls; MFA is enforced by the API and reflected in the UI.

screens.title: My appointments
screens.summary: Personnel own-scope, mobile-first list of appointments assigned to the authenticated personnel member only: date, service, status, start/end time, and the minimum masked client info needed to perform the appointment. No other personnel's schedule, no branch-wide search, no mutation actions, and no contact export.

screens.title: My queue
screens.summary: Personnel own-scope, mobile-first list of queue entries assigned to the authenticated personnel member only: position, status, service, labelled wait estimate, a preferred-request indicator, and the minimum masked client info needed to perform the work. No branch-wide queue, no staff selector, no mutation controls, and no contact export.

screens.title: My sessions
screens.summary: Personnel own-scope, mobile-first list of service sessions assigned to the authenticated personnel member only: status, service, start/completion time, and the minimum masked client info. No other personnel's sessions, no branch-wide list, no mutation actions, no contact export, and NO commission preview (earned/payable claims are never shown to Personnel).

screens.title: My Earnings
screens.summary: Personnel own-scope earnings: a per-currency overview (net/unpaid/paid, with salary and commission breakdowns shown only when the compensation model or historical facts apply; conflicting plans fail closed), compensation terms, payout history, on-demand earnings-statement generation/download through Servana's authorised short-lived file link (own-scope by owner; billing read-only blocks new generation, not an existing download), and raising an earnings query about one of the personnel's own facts (Finance responds; a correction is a separate adjustment). The acting staff profile is derived from the membership — there is no staff selector and the browser never sends a staff reference. No other staff data, no payout controls, no money movement, no raw storage paths, no Wallet/provider UI.

screens.title: Client SMS composer
screens.summary: Personnel own-scope bulk SMS to clients this staff member PERSONALLY SERVED (at least one completed service session performed by them, in the acting merchant + branch). The screen shows a paginated, name-searchable served-client list with MASKED contact only (`••• ••• 1234`), recipient selection bounded by the configured max batch, a composer whose character count, segment count, excluded-recipient reason codes and estimated KES cost all come from the server preview (the browser derives none of them), a billing notice, an explicit confirmation dialog, and the resulting campaign statuses with per-recipient outcomes. The acting staff profile is derived from the membership — there is no staff selector and the browser never sends a staff reference, a cost or a recipient count. The served-client READ (`personnel.my_served_clients.view`) survives billing read-only grace; SENDING (`personnel.my_sms.send`) additionally requires the `sms` plan entitlement and is blocked in read-only grace / suspended billing, with both refusals rendered as actionable copy rather than raw codes. NO contact export exists anywhere on this screen — no export, download, print, clipboard-copy or phone-list control, no full phone in state, storage or a URL, and no such control may ever be added (ADR-010; Plan §19.4 non-overridable).

screens.title: Platform billing settings
screens.summary: Contract page §5.4.3. Platform-wide billing configuration: the three canonical billing modes, effective-dated settings versions, trial, grace, overdue and suspension boundaries, and the percentage platform-fee configuration. Composes the shipped Phase 20A and 20E sections unchanged; approved terms are immutable, so a change supersedes rather than edits. Plans, prices, promotions and preferred-personnel fees are now contract pages of their own.

screens.title: Wallet configuration
screens.summary: Wallet integration configuration (webhook keys, breaker, inbox replay).

screens.title: Billing reconciliation exceptions
screens.summary: Masked billing reconciliation exceptions resolved via Wallet-orchestrated billing.

screens.title: Platform reports
screens.summary: Contract page §5.4.17. The platform reporting catalogue (Plan §69) is owned by Phase 21N, which Plan §80.1 makes dependent on Phase 20D-W, which is behind External Gate W. The contract report set is majority Wallet-derived, so a report page delivered now would misreport platform revenue and recovery. Platform AUDIT is a separate, implemented contract page (§5.4.18).

screens.title: Platform governance dashboard
screens.summary: Contract page §5.4.1. One SERVER-side aggregate read (GET /api/v1/platform/dashboard) over registrations, merchant lifecycle, commercial configuration, billing operations, audit and integrations. The browser computes no total: every other platform read is paginated, so a client-side aggregation over page one would misreport the platform on the very screen used to govern it. The integrations section renders External Gate W, never a zero and never a healthy state.

screens.title: Plans and entitlements
screens.summary: Contract page §5.4.4. Subscription plan metadata and the SERVER-enforced entitlements attached to each plan. Selecting a plan reveals its entitlements on the same page. Retiring a plan preserves existing subscription history, and nothing selected here creates a frontend-only restriction.

screens.title: Plan prices and billing periods
screens.summary: Contract page §5.4.5. Effective-dated plan prices across the five billing intervals. Overlapping effective ranges are rejected server-side, only future prices are cancellable, and current and historical prices are read-only so an issued invoice can never be rewritten.

screens.title: Promotional discounts
screens.summary: Contract page §5.4.6. Percentage or fixed-amount promotions with deterministic targeting. At most ONE discount applies to a subscription issuance, resolved server-side by the settled precedence order (merchant beats plan, plan beats billing mode, billing mode beats global), and an applied discount is captured as an immutable snapshot on the invoice it affected. Shares the Phase 20C form with free-period offers through a single-concern prop rather than a duplicated implementation.

screens.title: Free-period offers
screens.summary: Contract page §5.4.7. Free-period offers with the same deterministic targeting, lifecycle and immutability rules as promotional discounts, rendered through the same shared Phase 20C form. Draft, approve, pause, resume and cancel each require a mandatory reason, MFA and a fresh server-enforced step-up.

screens.title: Preferred personnel fee rules
screens.summary: Contract page §5.4.8. Fixed or percentage preferred-personnel fee rules at platform-default or per-service scope. Rules supersede rather than edit, so a rule that priced a past booking stays intact; approve and cancel require MFA and a fresh step-up.

screens.title: SMS billing settings
screens.summary: Contract page §5.4.9 (COR-UI08-001). Effective-dated platform SMS billing rules, per-merchant usage and charge reconciliation. A rule that has priced a segment is immutable: a change is a scheduled successor, and a scheduled rule may be cancelled before it takes effect. The page shows no recipient, no message body and no contact list, because SMS recipient export does not exist anywhere in Servana.

screens.title: Subscription operations
screens.summary: Contract page §5.4.13 (COR-UI08-001). Platform-wide monitoring of subscriptions, subscription invoices, billing credits and escalations over seven READ projections. There is no mutation of any kind: no record-payment, mark-paid, edit-invoice, override-state, create-credit or query-provider control exists, because a subscription state is changed by the billing lifecycle and an issued invoice is immutable.

screens.title: Registration monitoring
screens.summary: Contract page §5.4.10. Chronological self-registration feed with operational status, billing status and setup status shown separately, filtered by the one status parameter the shipped read allowlists, paginated from the server, and deep-linking to each merchant. There is NO approve, activate, create-merchant, first-administrator or KYC control, and none exists in the API. Risk indicators, duplicate-business warnings, velocity, IP and device metadata, referral anomalies and governance-note history have no backing field and are named as unavailable rather than rendered.

screens.title: Merchant directory
screens.summary: Contract page §5.4.11. Platform-wide directory of self-registered merchants. A row is a LINK to the merchant detail route, so a merchant record can be opened, bookmarked and shared; there is no embedded detail pane and no governance control here. No create-merchant, first-administrator, impersonation, membership, branch-creation or staff-creation control exists. Search, the plan, billing-mode, trial-cohort, overdue and risk filters, saved filters and a masked export have no backing operation and are named as unavailable rather than offered.

screens.title: Merchant detail and governance
screens.summary: Contract page §5.4.12. Governs one merchant, resolved from the route ULID on mount and on every parameter change, never from a row selected in the directory. Operational status and billing status are two separate, prominently labelled cards, and a governance action changes the operational status ONLY: a billing suspension is cleared by the billing lifecycle, never by reactivation here. Suspend, reactivate and deactivate each require a mandatory reason, an impact preview, explicit confirmation, MFA and a fresh server-enforced merchant_governance step-up. An unknown and a refused merchant render the SAME message, so a URL cannot enumerate the platform. No impersonation, setup completion, branch or staff creation, invoice, payment, receipt or queue action exists.

screens.title: Platform audit
screens.summary: Contract page §5.4.18. The append-only platform governance, billing, integration, security and administrative chain (merchant_id IS NULL), filtered by action, severity, actor, date and sort order, paginated, with a readable before-and-after view of the masked context and the correlation identifier. Read-only by contract: audit_logs rejects UPDATE and DELETE at the database level and no endpoint accepts either. No chain-integrity indicator is rendered because no endpoint exposes one, and no export control is offered because platform.audit.export is planned and owned by Phase 23 while the shipped audit exports are branch-scoped merchant exports.

screens.title: Internal platform access
screens.summary: Contract page §5.4.19 (COR-UI08-001). Invitation, permission and lifecycle management for internal Citrus platform users only. A platform user can never be given a merchant role, merchant membership, branch assignment or staff profile. Self-escalation is refused, the last active administrator cannot be removed or suspended, and every sensitive action requires MFA and a fresh step-up.

screens.title: Platform feature flags
screens.summary: Contract page §5.4.20 (COR-UI08-001). Maker and checker feature-flag governance with an append-only history. A flag can never grant a permission, bypass an entitlement, bypass a billing state or open an external gate: it only enables or disables an already-authorized capability.

screens.title: Account and security
screens.summary: Contract page §5.4.22. The signed-in Super Administrator own identity, two-factor enrollment and recovery codes, active sessions with remote revocation, and display preferences. Every endpoint it calls is own-scope and carries no user identifier, and a foreign session identifier returns 404 rather than 403. Management of other platform users belongs exclusively to internal platform access. There is no password, one-time-code login or passkey control, because Servana authenticates with Magic Links only, and no control here can lower the platform two-factor requirement.

screens.title: Platform fees
screens.summary: Merchant-wide masked platform-fee visibility (server earned summary per currency; fee-entry list/detail with ULID references, canonical tier label, rate and integer amounts, status) plus a dispute list and capability-gated create. Server-side merchant scope; no configuration, review, or reversal controls. Amounts are server-authoritative and the browser never recomputes fee money. No Wallet/settlement UI.

screens.title: Platform fees
screens.summary: Branch-attributable, read-only platform-fee visibility. The backend server-scopes entries to the actor assigned branches; no merchant-wide aggregate, no dispute or configuration controls. No Wallet/settlement UI.

screens.title: Platform fees
screens.summary: Finance platform-fee reconciliation view plus the dispute worklist: start review, resolve with an optional signed money change that creates an additive adjustment on a future invoice, and reject. Fresh step-up, period-lock and maker/checker are enforced by the API. The original ledger fact and issued invoices are never rewritten; there is no direct ledger edit or generic adjustment creator. No Wallet/settlement UI.

screens.title: Compensation liabilities
screens.summary: Finance masked, merchant-scoped compensation-liability surface: a per-currency summary (net salary, net commission, adjustments, combined net, plus gross accrual/earned and reversal totals; never combined across currencies), a filtered/paginated liability-entry list (salary accrual/reversal, earned commission/reversal) with safe source detail, a compensation-adjustment list/detail, and a capability-gated Record-adjustment dialog that posts a standalone additive positive/negative adjustment (server-derived branch/type/actors; fresh step-up + Idempotency-Key enforced by the API). The browser never computes authoritative liability money and never sends a server-owned field. A liability is not a payout, settlement, disbursement, earnings statement or paid event; no Wallet/provider UI.

screens.title: Platform fees
screens.summary: Masked, branch-scoped, read-only platform-fee visibility for Audit. No dispute-create or review controls, and no mutation anywhere. No private client contact, raw payment references, internal ids, or evidence content is shown. No Wallet/settlement UI.

screens.title: Global search
screens.summary: Cross-domain search over the records the authenticated user can ALREADY reach (Plan §68). A single term queries a fixed catalogue of document types — clients, staff, appointments, queue entries, service sessions, invoices, receipts, and a Personnel member's own served clients — and each type is admitted only after the server proves the caller holds the authority governing that type's own list/detail route (decision D-22-01). The screen therefore lists no permission of its own: `GET /api/v1/search` grants access to nothing, and a role with no searchable authority sees the empty state rather than a 403, which would confirm which types exist. Every filter is built server-side from the authenticated membership — the browser sends only the term and, optionally, a type list, an own-branch narrowing filter, an allowlisted sort and a bounded limit; the 21 scope/permission/engine forgery fields are rejected with 422. Results are masked by omission: the response schema has NO contact field of any kind — no phone, masked phone, phone last four, email or masked email — even for the types whose own Resources return masked contact today (decision D-22-03). An authorized EXACT phone lookup exists for Front Office through the existing keyed blind index, returns the client name only, never reaches the search engine, and never echoes the number back; a partial phone fragment is not searchable anywhere. NO export, download, print or clipboard-copy control exists on this screen and none may ever be added (ADR-010; Plan §19.4 non-overridable); nothing is persisted to localStorage or sessionStorage; and held results are cleared on any membership or branch-scope change.

screens.title: Public FAQ
screens.summary: The resolved account host's own compiled FAQ, rendered through SvFaq with the source's category dividers preserved. Host-derived: no path segment selects the account.

screens.title: Public legal document
screens.summary: The resolved account host's own Data Policy, Privacy Policy or Terms of Service, verbatim, at a role-free path. The document slug is one of three fixed values matched by the route.
